text:
The Jack Eichel trade turned five this month, and Buffalo and Las Vegas papers both marked it. The Golden Knights have the answer on their side: a Stanley Cup in 2022-23, and a center Evolving-Hockey rated sixth among 401 forwards last season at 3.5 wins above replacement.

This season he has 23 points in 18 games with 20 minutes a night of top-line work. Vegas controls 58.4 percent of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, and he remains one of the league's best passers: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.0 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 98th percentile among forwards.

There is a softer layer underneath. His team has scored 10.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his last ten games produced 10 points on 11.4 expected. That is still a very good player having a normal stretch. Our projection puts him around 94 points, with his ice time down a bit lately (19:34 over the last ten). One fun split: the Massachusetts native has 24 points in 22 career games against Boston.
headline: Five years after the trade, Eichel is still the engine
